articles.title_orig: Take a look inside the 'never-ending' Villa Vie Residences Odyssey cruise ship stranded in Cambodia
articles.title_zh: Take a look inside the 'never-ending' Villa Vie Residences Odyssey cruise ship stranded in Cambodia
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
A US Cruise ship stranded in Cambodia in the midst of an around-the-world trip asked passengers for money to refuel, it has been claimed, as reports suggest crew members working on board the Odyssey still haven’t been paid.
Lynn Montoya, who is travelling on the three-year trip alongside her husband Paul, said residents on board the cruise ship were repeatedly asked to contribute additional money for fuel and other expenses, including a call to raise funds for fuel to leave Cambodia.
Lynn said crew members working on the ship had also not been paid amid a lack of funds and soaring fuel costs.
“We were tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money for fuel, money for everything,” she said. “We had hopes, but they just kept sinking further and further into the hole through mismanagement.”
The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a trip intended to go around the world, with suite prices starting at around $230,000 (£172,000), but ran into trouble in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, after running out of fuel. For now, it remains docked in Cambodia with no certain departure date.
Guests were told at 6am on Monday that they had to disembark by 2pm that day. The cruise ship has capacity for 650 passengers, but 203 were on board - mostly Americans - when it suspended operations. There were also 156 crew members on board the ship.
Villa Vie Residences, the Florida-based operator of the MV Odyssey, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that used to average around $1,800 (£1352) , have skyrocketed to $6,000-$8,000 (£4,000-£6,000) in parts of Asia due to the ongoing war in Iran.
Traffic has largely been suspended in the Strait of Hormuz, an essential shipping lane transporting a vast proportion of the world’s oil, putting a major strain on fuel prices and sharply increasing costs - especially in Southeast Asia.
The cruise liner firm tried to decrease its fuel consumption by slowing down the itinerary and spending more time docked in port, but ultimately was unable to curb soaring fuel prices.
In a statement on Tuesday, Ville Vie Residences said: “We have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses.
“Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution. Our focus is now supporting residents, crew and employees. The company is working with residents to coordinate disembarkation and identify temporary living arrangements.”
Lanette Canen and Johan Bodin were among hundreds of guests who looked forward to a new life at sea when they boarded residential world cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey in October 2024.
The 56-year-olds sold a business to fund a $100,000 (£75,000) cabin on the ship – plus monthly maintenance fees of $3,500 (£2,633). Lanette ran a windshield-replacement company from the ship, and the pair documented their journey on their Living Life on a Cruise YouTube channel.
The couple said they knew leaving was possible because rumours had circulated on the ship about financial difficulties, but the eight-hour notice still surprised them.
Lanette said: “Our immediate reaction was a deep sense of heartbreak at having to leave the home and community we had built over the past two years.
“It was difficult to process the news while packing up our life and saying goodbye to the place we had come to love.”
She said Villa Vie helped unload suitcases and provided shuttles to and from the port, but it has not helped with paying for hotels.
Lanette said a fellow resident has offered to help others struggling financially with lodging costs and is working to arrange a charter flight to San Francisco.
She said: “Villa Vie has not given us a date for returning onboard. Regardless of whether operations resume, we have decided to move on. The company was planning to increase our maintenance fees, which would have priced us out.”
The couple now plan to stay at a hotel in Sihanoukville for about a week, then spend some time in Phnom Penh, and travel to Vietnam, Bali in Indonesia, and Thailand, where they hope the lower cost of living will help sustain their lifestyle while they figure out their longer-term plans.
Lanette said: “We’re doing well, considering everything, but we are heartbroken. There have been many hugs and tears. We loved our two years aboard, the adventures, the friendships, and especially the community. Many residents are settling together off the ship, so those connections are continuing on land.”
Other residents have complained about a lack of communication and support from the cruise line. One former resident, Sharon Lane , who had to leave the ship last year due to health issues, says her friends on board have been left confused.
She told The Independent : “There seems to be confusion as to what is being provided to residents.
“Communication has been an ongoing issue. I am very concerned for my friends. They need to figure out transport, visas, housing; it is very stressful. It took me weeks to arrange my departure, and they [only] had a few hours.”
Sharon still owns a cabin on the ship because her contract terms don’t let her rent it out, and a sale now looks unlikely.
She added: “I’ve lost money; everyone who owns has or will lose money. It is devastating for some who sold their own properties to fund this. It breaks my heart. I hope the owners of the ship keep the interests of the residents in mind.”
The Independent has contacted Villa Vie Residences for further comment.

articles.title_orig: United States and Japan forge missile production alliance to counter China's power
articles.title_zh: United States and Japan forge missile production alliance to counter China's power
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
The United States and Japan have agreed to establish a production facility in Japan to jointly manufacture advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles , according to the Japanese defense chief.
The decision marks the latest step by the two allies to bolster security capabilities amid heightened concerns over China 's growing military assertiveness across Asia.
Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi announced the agreement during a news conference Wednesday evening in Cebu, a province in the central Philippines .
His remarks followed a bilateral meeting with U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on the sidelines of an annual gathering of Southeast Asian defense chiefs and their major Asian and Western counterparts.
During a session on Thursday, Koizumi highlighted increased Chinese naval presence near southwestern Japan, noting that three Chinese destroyers alongside a coast guard vessel recently passed through the Osumi Strait south of Kyushu into the Pacific Ocean.
He stated that it was the first time his ministry had recorded such a fleet configuration.
Koizumi pointed to the transit as "an example illustrating the challenging security environment in the region," adding that Tokyo will maintain close surveillance of Chinese naval operations while continuing to accelerate its own military buildup in southwestern Japan.
The annual meetings aim to prevent major conflict and deepen regional cooperation, though the U.S., China, and their respective allies frequently exchange criticisms during the proceedings.
The joint manufacturing effort, titled "Operation Supercharge," will establish a final assembly and inspection plant in Japan for the Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile, or AMRAAM.
Koizumi emphasized that these missiles are essential for F-35 stealth fighters, which are operated by both the U.S. and Japanese militaries.
Recounting his meeting with Hegseth, Koizumi said he "shared a sense of crisis … regarding the increasingly severe regional situation and we agreed to strengthen the deterrence and response capabilities of the Japan-U.S. alliance with greater speed and intensity than ever before."
He added: "We reaffirmed the importance of a free and open international order based on the rule of law, which rejects any attempts to unilaterally alter the status quo through the use of force, coercion or other means."
In a separate meeting with ASEAN defense ministers led by Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr., Hegseth offered renewed assurances regarding Washington's commitment to regional stability.
Without calling out Beijing by name, Hegseth outlined the U.S. approach.
"The approach we’re taking, we describe as strong, quiet and clear," Hegseth told the defense chiefs, adding it is "Strong enough to deter coercion and aggression, quiet enough to avoid needless escalation or public theatrics to let our actions speak for themselves."
He emphasized that the position is "clear enough that our friends, our partners and potential adversaries understand precisely where the United States stands and that we will defend our interests and the interests of our allies and partners."
Hegseth reassured the Philippines, Washington’s oldest treaty partner in Asia, that the Trump administration will maintain robust deterrence against Beijing’s actions in the South China Sea, a critical trade waterway claimed almost entirely by China.
Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles pledged that Australian forces, alongside allies like the U.S., would continue upholding international law despite Chinese actions in disputed waters.
Referring to an incident last year where a Chinese J-16 jet released flares near an Australian P-8 Poseidon surveillance plane, Marles said: "That doesn’t deter us from doing what we need to do and that’s essentially asserting the rules-based order here in the end of the Pacific."
He added: "Freedom of navigation on the high seas is profoundly important for Australia."
Territorial claims in the South China Sea remain contested among the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei, and Taiwan, with frequent standoffs involving Chinese and Philippine coast guard and naval vessels.
Washington maintains that it is bound by treaty to defend the Philippines if Filipino forces, ships, or aircraft come under armed attack. Separately, Tokyo and Beijing remain locked in a maritime dispute over Japanese-controlled islands in the East China Sea.

articles.title_orig: DoorDash stock pops, Instacart falls after companies announce $17 billion acquisition deal
articles.title_zh: DoorDash stock pops, Instacart falls after companies announce $17 billion acquisition deal
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
DoorDash ( DASH ) announced plans to acquire hyperlocal grocery delivery provider Instacart ( CART ) on Thursday morning in a deal valued at $17 billion.
DoorDash, which is primarily known for its restaurant food delivery business, will pay $65 per Instacart share, a 26% premium over the stock's Oct. 22 closing price. The transaction includes 75% cash, with Instacart stockholders able to elect cash, DoorDash stock, or a combination of both. Instacart's board of directors unanimously approved the deal, according to a press release.
"Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online," DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in the release. "Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery."
DoorDash stock popped over 5%, while Instacart stock fell 1.5%.
The acquisition comes as Walmart ( WMT ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) have been taking share of the grocery delivery market, especially for same-day and one-hour delivery.
Prior to the announcement, Wedbush analyst Ygal Arounian said the combination of Instacart and DoorDash could "potentially prove to be a competitive differentiation."
"A combination of strong restaurant delivery plus a marketplace including various grocers from Instacart can be a critical combination against Walmart and Amazon in particular, who continue to push in this market as well," Arounian said.
Walmart currently holds a roughly 30.9% share of the online grocery market, ahead of Amazon at roughly 23.6%, per Wedbush.
For customers worried about what the Instacart acquisition means for prices, the company said shoppers will now get two memberships for the price of one and more choices.
"Instacart customers could shop at more than 50,000 additional stores, on top of the nearly 100,000 stores on the Instacart platform today," the release said.
For local business owners, the company said this would allow them more ways to earn.

articles.title_orig: Russian drone strike kills 14 on Ukrainian rail platform
articles.title_zh: Russian drone strike kills 14 on Ukrainian rail platform
articles.content_orig:
At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials have said.
Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.
Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a passenger train headed for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit.
Russia's military has not publicly commented. It has repeatedly hit Ukraine's large railway network, but Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians.
In Dnipro, an elevated threat level was announced ahead of Thursday's strike, according to the railway operator chief, Oleksandr Pertsovsky.
"But unfortunately there were still a large number of people on the platform" when the drone struck, he said.
Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov said the incident was a tragedy, adding that a drone hit an electric civilian train.
Pictures from the Ukrainian rescue services show a large hole in a platform that is strewn with blurred-out bodies, near a blast-damaged train with smashed windows.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said "the Russians used a drone to attack a platform where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing."
He called for further US, European and G7 sanctions on Russia and repeated his criticism of a controversial deal that was struck earlier this month between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which eased some sanctions on Moscow, allowing the US to import Russian diesel.
Elsewhere in Ukraine, two girls aged 15 were killed in a Russian missile attack on the centre of Chernihiv city, in the north of the country, regional head Vyacheslav Chaus said. At least 25 others, including four children, were injured, he added.
A day of mourning has been declared for Chernihiv and Dnipro on Friday.
In the city of Kremenchuk, in the central Poltava region, three people were killed and 28 injured in a Russian drone attack that hit residential buildings and a school, regional head Vitaliy Diakivnych said.
The latest Russian strikes came during efforts to uphold a fragile ceasefire in the besieged city of Oleshky, which has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have been trapped without food, water, medicine and electricity for years.
Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, wrote on Telegram that the truce was holding into a third day.
Meanwhile, the Kremlin has condemned Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow whilst the city hosts the Russia-Africa Summit, the Tass news agency has reported. The two-day event is attended by African leaders and government delegations from 48 countries.
The mayor of Moscow said 613 Ukrainian drones were launched overnight towards the region, most of which were shot down during their flight.
Russia's defence ministry has always denied targeting Ukrainian civilians and says its attacks on railways target the infrastructure used to transport military personnel and equipment.
However, the dangers to passengers are very real, and attacks on Ukraine's train infrastructure have risen sharply.
Of the 521 locomotives hit since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, almost 60% have been hit this year, according to statistics released by Ukrzaliznytsia supplied to AFP news agency.
Overall attacks on railway facilities have risen from 1,206 in 2025 to 1,700 so far this year.
There appears to have been a wider assault on Ukraine's infrastructure in recent weeks, with two bridges attacked in the capital Kyiv, and a metro train hit during one of the strikes.

articles.title_orig: SpaceX Wins Target Lift On AI, Data Center Growth. But Is It A Buy?
articles.title_zh: SpaceX Wins Target Lift On AI, Data Center Growth. But Is It A Buy?
articles.content_orig:
The race to build artificial intelligence infrastructure is creating enormous new risks that could threaten financing for the data centers powering the artificial intelligence boom, according to Aon CEO Greg Case.
In an interview with CNBC Wednesday, Case warned that clustering billions of dollars of equipment and computing capacity in a small number of locations could make some projects difficult to insure, with consequences for developers seeking financing.
"If you create them and you build them on top of each other, you've created concentration risk in a way in which it makes it more difficult to get insurance," Case said.
"If it's more difficult to get insurance, that means the financing structure is going to change completely. You can't access the debt markets," he said.
The potential financial exposure from operational disruptions is staggering, Case said.
"Data centers are literally going to measure business interruption at millions of dollars per minute," he told CNBC.
The warnings come as technology companies accelerate spending on data centers, electricity generation and other infrastructure needed to support AI. Those investments are creating opportunities for insurers, brokers and business risk consultants. They're also raising questions about whether traditional insurers have sufficient capacity to absorb the risks.
In its third-quarter earnings , Aon reported a record pipeline of data center projects, helping drive 7% organic revenue growth in its commercial risk business during the quarter. Adjusted earnings per share increased 10% to $3.36, while adjusted operating margin expanded 70 basis points to 27%. One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%.
The company has developed specialized insurance facilities, or pools of capacity to cover specific industries or risks, to address growing demand, including a $10 billion data center facility and a $2.5 billion energy facility.
Managing the risks begins well before a policy is written, according to Case. Aon said it is working with developers to design and locate facilities, reduce the potential for business interruption and structure insurance coverage that can support financing.
"These are engineering conversations around understanding risk," Case said.
The surge in demand for sophisticated risk management is also central to Aon's pending $17 billion acquisition of USI Insurance Services , which is expected to close in the fourth quarter.
The deal will combine USI with Aon's existing operations and NFP, which Aon acquired in 2024 , creating a roughly $6.5 billion middle-market platform.
Case said smaller companies face many of the same increasingly complex risks as multinational corporations, but often lack access to comparable analytics, expertise and insurance solutions.
"Our middle market clients have exactly the same challenges, exactly the same risks they face every day, and they deserve to have the content, the insight, the capability that the largest companies in the world have," Case said.
Most industry insiders and experts anticipate AI will make insurance brokerage and consulting more efficient. Asked why Aon is investing billions in acquisitions rather than exclusively expanding its technology capabilities, Case said the two are not mutually exclusive.
"This is about talent and technology," he said. "You get those both right. That's how you build the relationships that matter for clients."
Aon expects $395 million in annual earnings benefits from the USI combination, including $280 million in cost savings and $115 million in revenue synergies.
The acquisition will be financed with debt, and the company expects to prioritize reducing leverage over the next two years.
AI is creating opportunities for insurers to better understand vulnerabilities, even as the technology introduces new threats that could generate widespread financial losses.
Researchers disclosed two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language used by roughly 70% of websites, on Oct. 21. The flaws could allow hackers to remotely execute malicious code on vulnerable servers without authentication. AI played a significant role in discovering and analyzing the vulnerabilities through cybersecurity firms Calif and Google's Wiz, along with OpenAI.
Asked whether cyber risks are escalating faster than insurers can respond, Case said the industry needs to expand beyond its traditional capital base to meet growing demand.
"We have to keep up. We have to continue to evolve," he said.
Case estimates the global insurance industry currently has about $4.5 trillion in capital. He believes that amount must double or triple to meet the growing needs across cyber, AI, data centers and other emerging risks.
"Call it 5 trillion to 10 to 15 trillion," Case said, outlining his vision for expanding the industry's capacity and clarifying remarks he made in the company's second-quarter earnings call.
His strategy involves tapping institutional investors, pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and wealthy individuals to help finance risks traditionally carried by insurance companies and reinsurers. Case estimates those sources represent a potential pool of approximately $250 trillion in capital — a fraction of which could substantially expand the market.
Aon is increasingly positioning itself not simply as a broker connecting companies with existing insurers, but as an intermediary helping create new pools of capital to absorb complex risks.
"Not just being a market taker or market optimizer for our clients, but a market maker creating new markets to sort of drive and address risk," Case said.
That creates opportunities for alternative asset managers and private investors seeking returns from insurance-linked investments, although investors must be able to evaluate the potential for large and correlated losses.
Case said the critical ingredient is the ability to quantify exposures accurately enough to give investors confidence to commit their capital.
While corporate risk is becoming more complex, some commercial insurance prices are declining and companies are beginning to see some relief after years of rising premiums.
But, Case cautioned, this is not a prolonged period of lower insurance rates.
"Some are confusing that with it's a permanent soft market. Not the case at all," he said.
He said some corporate clients are using lower insurance prices as an opportunity to buy more protection rather than simply reduce spending.
"We have clients who literally, when they understand their exposure, even though the unit price might have been coming down, they completely restructure their program and buy more because they need more coverage," Case said.
The dynamic is helping Aon maintain growth despite softer pricing in commercial insurance and reinsurance markets.

articles.content_orig:
The Unesco-listed region is home to cone-shaped rock formations known as ‘fairy chimneys’, created by ancient volcanic activity
Three people, including a foreign national, were killed on Thursday when a rock spire collapsed in Turkey’s Unesco-listed Cappadocia region after a landslide triggered by heavy rain, officials said.
The region, a magnet for tourists from around the world, is home to cone-shaped rock formations known as “fairy chimneys”, created by ancient volcanic activity.
“According to initial findings, two people were killed and five others injured in the incident,” Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said on social media.

articles.title_orig: Fairy chimney rockfall kills two at Turkey's Cappadocia tourist attraction after heavy rain
articles.title_zh: Fairy chimney rockfall kills two at Turkey's Cappadocia tourist attraction after heavy rain
articles.content_orig:
Parts of a large volcanic rock formation crashed down in Turkey’s popular tourism destination of Cappadocia on Thursday, killing at least three people and injuring five others, officials said.
A section of the rock formation — known as a fairy chimney — tumbled in Cappadocia’s Goreme region, prompting authorities to deploy medical and rescue teams.
Gov. Huseyin Kok said recent heavy rains likely caused the collapse, which occurred near a parking lot at an entrance to the site.
He said rescue teams were continuing to search for other people who may be trapped under the debris.
“We hope that there are no other casualties,” the governor said. “We are deeply saddened.”
Kok said two of the three dead were Turkish nationals. He did not provide information on the third victim.
Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said an investigation was launched into the incident.
HaberTurk news channel showed heavy machinery removing chunks of rock from the foot of the formation.
Cappadocia, in central Turkey, is a UNESCO World Heritage-listed site famed for its distinctive rock formations and ancient underground cities. It is one of the country’s most visited tourism locations.
The collapse occurred on Turkey’s Republic Day holiday, when the area would have been crowded with visitors.

articles.content_orig:
On his 368th day without a job, Dia Harris woke at 8:30, slipped a coffee pod into his Keurig and checked his iPad to see how many more rejections had come in overnight.
There were two automated messages from “Meta Careers,” thanking him for applying to be a program manager. “Our recruiting team will contact you if your qualifications are a strong match,” Harris read. By his count, those were the 560th and 561st roles he’d sought since getting fired from the federal government.

(Photo: Zwift/Corie Spruill)
Video routes mean more routes Lots of new badges to chase Quality machine learning based structured training system Workouts use group rides and RoboPacers instead of just ERG mode Immediate post-ride coach analysis on pacing and fatigue
Requires an upgraded Zwift Plus premium subscription When deviating from the plan feedback is unclear
Today, Zwift is launching Zwift Plus. This new premium tier pushes the monthly cost to $29.99, with a discounted yearly option at $299.99. In exchange for the upcharge, you unlock two core upgrades: real-world video routes and adaptive coaching.
Zwift considers this a massive milestone, which is why I recently went to Moab to celebrate the video-based routes ahead of launch. The concept was to ride the route indoors, then ride it outdoors to see how perfectly they matched. Unfortunately, we caught the tail end of a Pacific hurricane, so I only got to drive the route and ride it inside. Still, the big reveal ended up feeling almost anti-climactic—but in the best way possible.
The inside perfectly matches the real world, but you still get all the Zwift details you are used to. Zwift lays the graphics seamlessly into high-resolution and high frame rate footage. I rode the Tron bike in Arches National Park, and while it sadly doesn’t glow on the road, the wheels sit perfectly on the video road and the speed adjusts as you ride without ever breaking the illusion. It’s underwhelming, but only because it’s really good and feels like a natural extension of what Zwift already does. If you’ve used Rouvy, which Zwift now owns, this is better.
Personally, though, I don’t find the video-based routes all that much of a draw. They provide more variety, and that’s great, but Zwift already adds routes all the time and anyone who’s used Zwift knows the team is great at recreating real-life locations. What this launch is really all about is coaching, and that’s where the real magic is.
Part of why the team at Zwift considered this launch such a high-stakes proposition is that it’s a price increase, and that always comes with baggage. You could even consider the addition of the video routes to the Zwift Plus plan as a sort of tiered pricing structure where, all of a sudden, you have to pay for more routes. That’s not really true, but I can understand the hesitation.
I think part of why I don’t see that as an issue is because I don’t find the video routes to be the major news here. They are additional content, and as someone who will likely chew through every single additional badge Zwift offers this winter, that’s nice, but also not a big deal. Instead, I see this as a pretty clear value proposition of $10 a month for structured training.
With that in mind, my favorite thing about Zwift Plus is that I see it as a product that is going to consolidate the structured training market. I believe this will be a big hit to TrainerRoad, and I think that for many people, Zwift Plus will represent a net decrease in monthly subscriptions.
The reasons for this are pretty simple: structured training has to be good enough, and it has to create an environment where the user actually follows the plan. Before this launch, Zwift was mostly failing at both of those requirements.
Zwift already had training plans; they just weren’t engaging, they weren’t reactive, and they were widely considered to be not that great. With Zwift Plus, the first correction was the quality of the plans, and to address that, Zwift brought on Ryan Cooper.
If you aren’t familiar with the name, Ryan Cooper is the founder of Best Bike Split and the former Chief Scientist at TrainingPeaks. To understand why his involvement is so important, you have to look at what Best Bike Split actually does. It is a predictive physics engine that takes a rider’s specific power profile, weight, and aerodynamics, layers it over the exact elevation of a race course, and calculates exactly how many watts that rider should push on every single segment to finish as fast as possible without blowing up.
That is the level of data-driven modeling he brings to Zwift, and it is exactly why the brand is very careful to call this new coaching system “machine learning” rather than “AI.” Right now, AI is a marketing buzzword. When most people hear it, they picture a chatbot scraping the internet and hallucinating a generic training plan based on a text prompt.
Machine learning is different. It relies on math and datasets. In this case, Cooper’s algorithms were trained on the anonymized power and heart rate data of millions of Zwift riders, combined with peer-reviewed sports science. The system isn’t guessing or estimating based on what it read online. It uses actual machine learning to recognize patterns in your specific history, power data, and daily fatigue, and then mathematically calculates exactly what you need to do today to actually get faster.
This means Zwift has now solved the quality problem that TrainerRoad has so far always held as an advantage. But the raw quality of workouts is actually somewhat secondary in real life. You need not only quality workouts, but you need workouts that people will complete, and this is where Zwift has something no one else does.
Zwift controls everything about where you ride your bike, and that means the Zwift Plus workout plan has options. Once you set up your plan, the system will recommend an ever-changing variety in terms of how you complete a workout. My favorite example was actually the first day of the 12-week plan I started, when I was scheduled for a route rather than a set of intervals.
Except, if you squinted a bit, you’d see a clear interval workout. The route was the Watopia Mountain Route, and while it might appear to be a free ride, the route starts with a few miles of flats, then it climbs for a while before descending and finishing with some flats. What is actually happening there is that you get about 8-10 minutes of warm-up, then you have a work block of about 40 minutes before you get a rest, and finally a 20-ish minute cool-down where you ride the flats again. And Zwift knows, based on all your past rides both inside and out, exactly how hard you will ride each of those sections. Except I actually went harder because I started late and wanted to finish faster, so in my case, I got a notice asking if I wanted to adjust my plan based on the new intensity.
In the first week, I also had traditional intervals and a follow-the-RoboPacer session. The result is a tight training plan that adapts to you if you don’t follow it exactly, but rarely looks like a tight training plan. It’s a sort of trick to keep you engaged, and my money is on it working very well.
The only problem with this system is that, at launch, there’s not enough AI and there’s not enough feedback. I am told some of this will come, but it’s not super clear when or how much, so I have to evaluate what exists right now—and right now, it needs more interaction.
I am sure many people will not want to hear that this should have a chatbot, but I think it should. It has to be a good one, but for more than a year now I’ve bounced around between different AI systems, and when it works, it’s incredibly helpful. For a long time, I used Google Gemini paired with Garmin Connect, and this summer I’ve been playing with RideWithDave. Whatever system I’ve used, the main benefit is that you can ask the robot about deviations. “I have this scheduled; what if I do this instead? Does that fulfill the same goal?” Or, the opposite happens plenty, too: “Hey, I had this scheduled but instead I did this; did I satisfy the goal?” With the Zwift system, you just have to guess.
And once you do guess, there’s very little feedback one way or the other. One day, I had an interval session scheduled that was 2×20

articles.title_zh: Gallery: Here's A Closer Look At The Zelda 40th Anniversary Special Edition Switch 2
articles.content_orig:
🎮 The Zelda 40th anniversary Switch 2 is out today, October 29, but Walmart and Target are planning online restocks for November 6
🚨 Our Zelda Switch 2 restock tracker @mattswider on X will send out an alert as soon as stock appears
👀 Walmart was our top pick to have a restock, but a supply chain delay has pushed the date back
⌚ GameStop, Best Buy, and Nintendo are holding in-store midnight launches where units will be available
Update (11:23 AM ET): Nintendo announced a restock at the Nintendo Store , though it seems to be flashing in and out of stock. We were able to add it our basket after a few tries.
Walmart: Zelda Switch 2 console
Best Buy: Zelda Switch 2 console
GameStop: Zelda Switch 2 console
Target: Zelda Switch 2 console
Nintendo: Zelda Switch 2 console
🚨 We’re tracking Zelda Switch 2 stock updates. If you’d like to know when more stock arrives, follow Matt Swider on X and turn on notifications. You can also become a free or paid subscriber to The Shortcut to help support our work. 🚨
A new update has dashed our hopes of a major Walmart restock of the Zelda Switch 2 console, which we were confident would happen today. However, a new Reddit post (thanks, Wario64 ) has revealed that Walmart is waiting until at least November 6 to sell the special edition console online.
🚨 Want the Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2? Drop your email for restock alerts before it sells out. ⤵️
A employee note says: “Due to a supply chain delay, some stores may not receive the Nintendo Switch 2 Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition in time for its planned Oct. 29 release. To allow time to fulfill preorders and reshop inventory as needed, the point-of-sale (POS) block will remain in place through at least Friday, Nov. 6. As inventory arrives, orders will be fulfilled based on preorder priority and available inventory.”
The Redditor who posted the news shared that some people were able to get the console from Walmart after 8:00am local time, so there is still hope.
Target recently updated its Zelda Switch 2 listing to reveal that it will also start taking orders of on November 6, with in stores orders beginning November 5. Clearly, the supply chain delay is impacting other stores, otherwise we likely would have seen a restock take place today, as we initially predicted.
We now know that Walmart and Target will be taking online orders, and that Best Buy and Nintendo are holding in-store events on November 5. GameStop is also letting customers pre-order in-store via their website .
Despite the news, we’ll still be tracking every retailer with our restock tracker, which provides up-to-the-second information whether something is in stock. If the Zelda Switch 2 does appear – which it might – our followers will still be one of the first to know.

articles.title_orig: Serious pollution by water industry remains high despite £5bn investment, say regulators
articles.title_zh: Serious pollution by water industry remains high despite £5bn investment, say regulators
articles.content_orig:
South West Water has been given the lowest possible environmental rating by the Environment Agency over high levels of pollution.
The regulator downgraded the firm from two stars out of a possible four to one, meaning it is now considered a "poor performing company" for its environmental impact.
It said it had performed "significantly below target" for sewage pollution incidents for the 15th year in a row.
South West Water, which has 1.8 million customers across Devon, Cornwall, the Isles of Scilly and parts of Dorset and Somerset, said it knew there was "much more to do" and was taking action to improve areas that "matter most" to customers and the environment.
The annual Environmental Performance Assessment grades England's nine water and sewerage companies largely on how often they pollute rivers, streams and the sea.
For 2025, South West Water was among four companies rated as poor performing, or one star, while four others were rated as requiring improvement, two stars.
South West Water performed "significantly below target" for sewage pollution incidents [BBC]
Severn Trent Water was the only company to achieve the highest rating of four stars.
The Environment Agency's report card comes a month after South West Water was fined almost £8m for a series of pollution-related offences over six years.
In the last year it also recorded the sharpest rise in customer complaints of any water company .
Serious incidents in the past year include pollution in St Austell River , killing thousands of fish, while pollution at Exmouth meant beachgoers had to leave the water .
Industry regulator Ofwat said the company met seven of its 23 targets in 2025-26, with below target performance for "most areas".
It noted its performance in relation to water supply interruptions "deteriorated substantially" and, despite improving annual performance by 38%, said the company's total pollution incidents performance remained more than double its target.
Customer satisfaction also remained challenging, ranking 15 out of 17 in the sector.
While storm overflows performance improved by 19%, it still fell short of its target, the Environment Agency said.
It was, however, the only company to have met its target for internal sewer flooding, or how often wastewater enters a property, every year since 2020-21.
A spokesperson for South West Water said: "We are under new management with a renewed focus on improving our performance.
"We know there's much more to do and although it will take time, we are taking action and making progress in the areas that matter most to our customers and the environment."
They said the firm had "reduced spills from storm overflows by 17% last year alone, with spill duration down by 25%, and we have insourced over 40 new leakage specialists".
"We are working hard to build on the progress we're making, backed by record levels of investment across the region," the spokesperson said.
"We are transforming our network to improve long-term resilience of our water supply; protecting the environment and tackling leaks as part of our multibillion-pound plan to deliver the long-term improvements our customers and communities expect."
People were advised against bathing at Exmouth after a pollution incident last year [BBC]
A separate report from the Drinking Water Inspectorate, the Environment Agency, Natural Resources Wales and Ofwat said South West Water's drinking water quality "remains exceptional, and consumers can be confident that their water is safe to drink".
It noted although its internal sewer flooding performance had deteriorated, "it is still performing better than the industry average".
However, it said overall environmental performance "is poor".
In a summary, the report said overall water supply interruptions "remain a significant concern, and it is one of the worst performers in the industry".
To improve the company needed to reduce interruptions and complete a transformation programme to address the root causes of its failures and "substantially improve customer interactions and overall experience", it said.
Surfers Against Sewage described the latest performance ratings as "another league of shame for water companies" but she added they were "a mere slap on the wrist that means absolutely nothing".
Head of campaigns Jo Morley said: "What is the point in these environmental performance ratings when year after year water company behaviour gets worse?"

articles.title_orig: Mongolian mining company says copper exports have dropped due to China border restrictions - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Mongolian mining company says copper exports have dropped due to China border restrictions - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
The operator of one of Mongolia’s largest copper mines says its exports of copper concentrate to China have dropped by about 70% in the past two weeks due to restrictions at a border crossing
ULAANBAATAR, Mongolia -- The operator of one of Mongolia’s largest copper mines said Thursday its exports of copper concentrate to China have dropped by about 70% in the past two weeks due to restrictions at a border crossing.
The restrictions have raised concerns over potential revenue losses and disruptions to Mongolia’s massive mineral sector.
Oyu Tolgoi LLC, which operates Oyu Tolgoi, one of the world’s largest copper mines, said the number of truck convoys transporting copper concentrate across the Chinese border has fallen from the usual 12 to 13 per day to just around four. The restrictions affect vehicles crossing at China’s Ganqimaodu Border Port, which is adjacent to Mongolia’s Gashuunsukhait Border Port.
The export cuts amount to a decline of about $300 million compared to normal operating conditions and could reach $1.2 billion if restrictions continue through the end of the year, local media reported on Wednesday.
Oyu Tolgoi LLC did not confirm the reported losses in a statement to The Associated Press on Thursday.
Mongolia is a major supplier of coal and copper to China, the world’s largest consumer of both commodities.
Mongolian border officials said the slowdown was related to infrastructure and technology upgrades at China’s Ganqimaodu Border Port.
Authorities in China’s Inner Mongolia region did not immediately answer questions from the AP.
In August, Chinese authorities introduced an in-vehicle facial recognition system for truck drivers crossing the border, and installation and maintenance work have affected border processing capacity, according to the Mongolian border authorities.
Mongolia’s government said the Chinese embassy in Ulaanbaatar informed it that the work, originally due to end by late September according to Mongolian news reports, may continue until the end of December.
Mongolian Finance Minister Mendsaikhan Zagdjav said some ministers were instructed during a Cabinet meeting to visit the border crossing and meet with Chinese authorities, according to local news reports.
All transport routes on the Mongolian side remain open and the government was not aware of any political reasons behind the restrictions, said the minister of Road and Transport, Delgersaikhan Borkhuu.
Mongolia’s copper sector has become an increasingly important contributor to national export revenues. During the first nine months of 2026, copper concentrate exports reportedly reached 2 million tons.
The border crossing restrictions have also affected Mongolia’s coal exports through Gashuunsukhait, with the number of vehicles crossing falling to just over 1,000 a day from 1,300 a day, border authorities said.
Mongolia has abundant mineral resources, including coal, copper, gold, uranium and fluorspar, and its economy relies heavily on mining, which accounts for roughly a quarter of its GDP. It is particularly sensitive to disruptions to cross-border trade and fluctuations in commodity prices.
Last year, coal and copper concentrates together accounted for 82.3% of Mongolia’s merchandise exports, while 89.4% of total exports went to China. Mongolia was also China’s leading supplier of imported coking coal, accounting for approximately 51% of Chinese coking coal imports in 2025.
